newsitem.title: GERMANY: Paris says not ready to put back satellite project.
newsitem.headline: Paris says not ready to put back satellite project.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon was quoted on Monday as saying Paris was not prepared to postpone a joint project to build a new spy satellite which Bonn is having trouble financing.

France wants to make Europe less dependent on United States intelligence by building the Helios 2 satellite, and sees the project, which Chancellor Kohl agreed to in talks with President Jacques Chirac, as a flagship of Franco-German cooperation.
But German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe says he cannot afford Bonn's share of the satellite from his 1997 budget, cut four percent from its planned level as part of an austerity programme.
Asked by the Stuttgarter Zeitung newspaper if Paris was prepared if necessary to put back a decision to go ahead with Helios 2, Millon said "No, no, no".
He said he understood Ruehe's budget problems but added: "I can only say there is an agreement between the Chancellor and the President."
Ruehe has said his top priority is the Eurofighter aircraft, which Germany needs to replace its ageing fleet of warplanes.

The news weekly Der Spiegel said Kohl had instructed top officials in several ministries to produce a long-term funding plan before December aimed at finding a way to go ahead with Helios 2 despite Ruehe's opposition.

Kohl and Chirac hold a regular six-monthly summit in December, and are due to discuss a Franco-German commission's evaluation of 26 joint arms projects in the light of spending cuts in both countries.

Defence sources say the German military, which is much less likely to be sent on missions abroad than French forces, needs new transport helicopters and a large transport aircraft more urgently than satellites, and cannot pay for them all.
Defence ministry experts estimate that Helios 2 and another planned joint intelligence satellite, Horus, would cost Germany 6 billion marks ($3.9 billion) between now and 2009. ($1=1.5306 Mark)
